description: Add a recommended visit route per beat using OSRM road-network routing (motorcycle profile). Supervisors trigger route generation from a beat list panel; routes are shown as numbered markers and a polyline on the map. Lasso reassignments clear stale routes. KML exports store stops in routed order.

userStories.title: Nearest neighbor TSP algorithm
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a nearest neighbor TSP function that takes a distance matrix and a starting index and returns the optimal store visit order so that beats can be routed efficiently.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/routing.ts exports function: nearestNeighborTSP(matrix: number[][], startIndex: number): number[]
Returns an ordered array of store indices of length N (one entry per store)
Every store index appears exactly once — no skips, no duplicates
Greedy nearest neighbor: at each step, picks the closest unvisited store using the matrix row of the current store
Works correctly for N=1 (returns [0]) and N=2 edge cases
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: OSRM route API endpoint
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a POST /api/route endpoint that calls the OSRM Table API to get road-network distances and returns an ordered store list so the client can render the route.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/route accepts JSON: { stores: Array<{ store_name: string, lat: number, long: number }> }
Computes beat centroid as mean of all store lat/lng values
Identifies starting store as the store with shortest Euclidean distance to the centroid
Calls OSRM Table API: GET https://router.project-osrm.org/table/v1/driving/{coords} where coords is 'lng,lat;lng,lat;...' (longitude first)
Applies nearestNeighborTSP() from lib/routing.ts using the OSRM durations matrix and the starting store index
Returns JSON: { orderedStores: Store[] } — stores sorted in visit sequence
Returns 500 with { error: string } if OSRM call fails (non-200, network error, or timeout)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Beat list panel UI
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want a beat list panel on the map view so I can see all beats and trigger route generation per beat.
acceptanceCriteria: A scrollable panel is visible alongside the Leaflet map on the dashboard, listing all beats
Each beat row shows: colored swatch matching beat color, Beat ID, GCU, store count, route status badge, and a 'Generate Route' button
Route status badge shows one of three states: 'Not routed' (gray), 'Routed ✓' (green), 'Error' (red)
When 'Generate Route' is clicked, that row shows a loading spinner and the button is disabled
Panel list updates automatically when beats change (e.g. after lasso reassignment)
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Route visualization on map
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want to see routed beats drawn on the map with numbered markers and a connecting polyline so I can visually verify the route makes geographic sense.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking 'Generate Route' on a beat row calls POST /api/route with that beat's stores
On success: stores in the routed beat are displayed as numbered DivIcon markers (1, 2, 3...) colored to match the beat color, replacing the default circle markers for that beat
On success: a Leaflet Polyline is drawn connecting stores in visit sequence, colored to match the beat color
On success: beat row status updates to 'Routed ✓'
On error: beat row status updates to 'Error' with message 'Route failed — try again'; no markers or polyline drawn
All routed beats show their routes simultaneously on the map
Unrouted beats continue to show default circle markers
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Lasso tool route invalidation
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want routes to be cleared when I reassign stores via the lasso tool so I never review a stale route.
acceptanceCriteria: When stores are reassigned via the lasso tool, the route is cleared for both the source beat and the target beat
Both affected beats revert to 'Not routed' status in the beat list panel
Numbered markers and polyline for both affected beats are removed from the map; default circle markers are restored
Other beats' routes are unaffected by the reassignment
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: KML export in routed order
userStories.description: As a supervisor, I want the KML export to include stores in routed order so field agents follow the correct visit sequence in Google Maps.
acceptanceCriteria: When a beat has been routed, its Placemarks in the KML are written in visit sequence order (first store visited = first Placemark)
When a beat has NOT been routed, its stores are exported in the existing default order (no regression)
The routed order is passed from dashboard state to POST /api/kml — update the request payload to include orderedStores per beat where available
No other KML structure changes — ExtendedData fields, Style, colors, and folder structure remain identical
Typecheck passes
